scope_note: ITAM is an UMBRELLA domain. Children HAM (hardware), SAM (software), SMP (SaaS), FINOPS (cloud cost) own the asset-class specifics. This audit covers ONLY the genuinely cross-asset layer the umbrella must master: the unified contract/renewal register, cross-asset lifecycle log, normalized catalog/SKU records, portfolio/TCO rollup reporting, and asset disposal across types. Hardware-specific (warranties, spare parts), license-specific (entitlements, true-ups), SaaS-specific (app discovery, shadow IT), and cloud-cost (budgets, anomalies) entities are explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for the umbrella and are NOT reported as MISSING here.

surface_matrix.compliance_basis: Physical inventory verification / SOX asset existence

missing.reason: The renewal register is the single most-wanted umbrella surface for the mid-market IT-ERP buyer: a dated, statused projection of every cross-asset contract coming up for renewal. asset_contracts master exists but the renewal lifecycle/junction that drives 'what renews when, owned by whom' is absent. All 4 enterprise vendors model renewals as first-class.

Cross-asset contractual obligations (true-up dates, notice periods, SLAs, audit clauses, minimum commitments) tracked for audit-defense. ServiceNow/Flexera/USU all surface an obligations register distinct from the contract header.

PORTFOLIO-REPORTING module masters NOTHING (only consumes saas_applications). The whole point of the module is the cross-asset TCO rollup ('what do we own and what does it cost') and there is no entity to hold it. Rule #14 violation plus the headline umbrella value gap.
Per-asset cross-asset cost line (acquisition, recurring, support) feeding the TCO rollup. Without it the rollup has no inputs at the umbrella level.

NORMALIZATION-CATALOG module is entirely EMPTY. Its reason to exist is the normalized hardware+software catalog/SKU master (Flexera Technopedia, ServiceNow Content Library, USU Technology Catalog). The umbrella's normalization layer is wholly unbuilt.

The unified cross-asset register row ('the single what-do-we-own record') that the normalization module catalogs and that lifecycle events / cost records hang off. Every vendor masters a unified asset record spanning classes.
Normalized model/product definition (make/model/version) that asset_records resolve to. Core of the catalog/SKU normalization surface.

Cross-asset disposal/retirement with chain-of-custody and data-destruction evidence (ITAD). Explicitly the cross-asset disposal flow the umbrella owns. asset_lifecycle_events logs events but the disposition record with certificate/recovery-value is its own entity.
The cross-asset vendor/supplier master the contract register references. asset_contracts has no counterparty master to point at; every vendor models a supplier/vendor record at the contract layer.
Fixed-asset depreciation schedule for the financial TCO/book-value view. ServiceNow and USU surface it; SOX fixed-asset register relies on it.
Notification/alert entity for upcoming renewals and expirations. Common across all vendors; drives the proactive-renewal value prop. Lower priority than contract_renewals itself.
Physical-inventory / existence-verification audit events spanning asset classes (SOX asset existence). Present in Ivanti/ServiceNow/USU/Lansweeper.
Junction allocating asset cost to cost centers / org units / departments for chargeback at the portfolio level. Common in Flexera/ServiceNow/USU.

scope_creep.reason: saas_applications is an SMP-mastered (SaaS Management) entity. Held here as a consumer (role='consumer'), which is legitimate cross-domain dependency for the TCO rollup, NOT scope creep proper. Flagged only to confirm the role stays 'consumer'/'embedded_master' and never flips to 'master' on the umbrella. No action recommended.

purchase_orders is a procurement-domain master; held as role='consumer' here for the acquisition leg of the lifecycle. Legitimate consumer dependency, not creep. Confirm it never flips to master on the umbrella.
locations as embedded_master is the correct autonomous-deployable-unit shape (canonical master lives elsewhere). PASS, not creep. Listed only for completeness.
org_units as embedded_master is the correct shape. PASS, not creep.

recommendations.reason: The 4-module split is the RIGHT decomposition of the cross-asset umbrella and maps cleanly to how Flexera/Ivanti/ServiceNow/USU package it: a normalized catalog layer, a unified contract register, a unified lifecycle log, and a portfolio/TCO reporting rollup. Module NAMES self-explain to a first-time deployer. Do not merge/split. The problem is not the split; it is that 2 of the 4 modules are unbuilt.

Module 57 has ZERO data_objects - a Rule #14 hard failure (a full module must carry >=1 master). It must master normalized_catalog_entries + asset_records + asset_models + asset_categories. Until filled, the module is a non-deployable shell.

Module 60 masters NOTHING (only consumes saas_applications) - Rule #14 failure. It must master tco_rollups + asset_cost_records (+ depreciation_schedules). A reporting module that holds no rollup/cost record is the umbrella's biggest value gap for the IT-ERP buyer.

modularization.verdict_note: Verdict is 'partial' (NOT coherent): the split design is coherent, but 2 of 4 modules fail Rule #14 (zero-master / empty) and the contract register lacks its renewal+obligation surface. The umbrella does NOT yet deliver the single 'what do we own and what does it cost' view it is supposed to be.
